description:
FILED s473c (Opus, 2026-09-08), found by #1240's probe table (row `in-module`).
PRE-EXISTING; unchanged by #1240 with its gate on or off.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):

    use File::Basename ();
    eval { File::Basename::basename() };  print "[$@]";

    perl  [fileparse(): need a valid pathname at PROG.pl line 2.\n]
    PCL   [fileparse(): need a valid pathname\n]

CAUSE, and it is deliberate as written: lib/Carp.pm is a four-line shim --

    sub croak   { die join('', @_), "\n"; }
    sub confess { die join('', @_), "\n"; }
    sub carp    { warn join('', @_), "\n"; }
    sub cluck   { warn join('', @_), "\n"; }

The trailing "\n" is exactly perl's "do not append a location" marker, so the
message reaches $@ bare.  Every module that reports an argument error through
Carp -- which is most of CPAN and most of lib/ -- therefore prints a
diagnostic no perl program ever prints, and `$@ =~ /at \S+ line \d+/` fails
against it.

WHY #1240's LOCATION REGISTER DOES NOT FIX IT.  perl's croak reports the
location of the CALLER of the sub that called croak (confess reports a full
backtrace).  The register holds the CURRENT statement, which inside croak's
body is a line of Carp.pm -- the wrong answer, and the very reason croak
exists.  A fix needs a per-FRAME location stack: p-sub-frame already saves and
restores the pair (that is #1240's mechanism), so keeping the SAVED value
reachable -- one more slot beside *pcl-caller-pkg-stack* /
*pcl-caller-subname-stack*, which are already per-call -- would let croak read
its caller's caller.  That also gives `caller()` the file and line it still
stubs (docs/caller-implementation.md; ir-spec Â§7 calls file/line stubs).

SIZE IT FIRST, like #1240: a per-call PUSH is exactly the hot-path cost
#1240's measurement was about, so the shape to measure is "reuse the value
p-loc-save already reads" (it costs nothing extra) against "a real stack".


=== #1994 battery evidence (s492, Fable): b2-21 + ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/carp1.pl -- croak/carp/confess messages carry NO location at all (perl: ` at CALLER-FILE line N.`; confess: a 3-line trace, PCL 1 line).  `caller` itself is right (battery idiom goto-sub-caller == perl incl. line numbers), so the shim can build the short message from caller() today.  USER standing: exact fatal TEXT is not a goal unless cheap -- this one is cheap and it is the difference between a findable and an unfindable error.  Scheduled with the s492b module-surface batch.


=== ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED (s492c, 2026-09-21, Opus) -- DO NOT RETRY THE CHEAP SHAPE ===
The obvious cheap fix -- drop the trailing "\n" from croak/confess/carp/cluck
so that `die`'s own location machinery (#1240) appends " at FILE line N." --
was tried and REVERTED, because it makes the message WORSE, not better:

    use Carp; package M; sub boom { croak "bad arg" }
    package main; eval { M::boom() }; print $@;

    perl:              bad arg at PROG.pl line 10.        (the CALLER of boom)
    PCL without "\n":  bad arg at .../lib/Carp.pm line 35.
    PCL with "\n":     bad arg                            (today)

MEASURED, and this is the fact the task's "size it first" note wanted: the
#1240 location register IS LIVE INSIDE THE SHIM.  `lib/Carp.pm` is transpiled
like user code and its `die` statement runs its own `(p-line 35)`, so by the
time croak's body executes the register names Carp.pm.  A location pointing
into the diagnostic library is worse than none -- it sends the reader to the
wrong file.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEEDED, unchanged from the task's own sketch: a PER-FRAME
saved location, so croak can read its CALLER'S CALLER.  `p-sub-frame` already
saves the pair lexically (`p-loc-save` binds two fixnums), and
`*pcl-caller-pkg-stack*` / `*pcl-caller-subname-stack*` are already consed per
call -- so the shape to COST is a third parallel stack (one cons + one special
bind per sub call, on the hottest path in the runtime, which is why it must be
measured and not assumed), or carrying the location in the existing pkg-stack
entry.  `caller` itself would get the file and line it still stubs
(`caller(0)` answers the LISP file and line today -- probed: `caller1.pl`
prints /tmp/runpcl_NNN.lisp line 28).

Also measured while here: `die`/`warn` DO get the right perl file and line
(dieloc1.pl is identical to perl), so the register works; it is only the
frame-relative read that is missing.
subject: Carp's croak/confess/carp/cluck append a bare newline, so every module diagnostic loses perl's ` at CALLER line N.` -- and the caller's LOCATION is the one thing the #1240 register cannot supply
